Header line for a print method

Source: R/utils_print.R
pr_head.Rd

Print a class label on a solid background followed by a grey one-line summary: the first line of an S3 print method.

Usage

pr_head(class, ..., bg = "blue", fg = "br_white")

Arguments

class

Character. Label shown on the chip, usually class(x)[1].

...

Pieces of the summary, joined by a middle dot. NULL, NA and empty strings are dropped, so optional pieces can be passed as if (cond) "text". Numbers show as print() shows them, factors and dates as their labels. SPSS user-missing values are omitted; explicit missing factor levels remain as <NA>.

bg, fg

Background and text colour of the chip: anything cli::make_ansi_style() accepts, i.e. an ANSI colour name such as "blue" or "br_white", an R colour name or a hex code. Without colour (knitted documents, log files) the label prints as <class>.

Value

The printed line, invisibly.

Details

A line longer than the console is cut with an ellipsis.

See also

Other print helpers: pr_badge(), pr_box(), pr_kv(), pr_note(), pr_section(), pr_spark(), pr_table(), pr_tree()

Examples

pr_head("sens_res", 'method = "cox"', "tipr 1.0.2", "n = 2,314")
#>  sens_res  method = "cox" · tipr 1.0.2 · n = 2,314
